messages:
Paula Mendes: Heads up: we’ve had a bunch of questions coming in about the new “usage insights” work.

Paula Mendes: Quick Q&A thread here for everyone: what does “route” mean in this context, how should people name it, and where should folks send feedback/edge cases.

Dev Patel: +1, support is already getting “what is a route?” and “why do I see Unknown route?” questions.

Logan Wright: Route = a customer-defined identifier that groups requests the way *you* think about your app endpoints/workflows.

Logan Wright: Think “/api/chat” or “checkout/estimate_shipping” etc. Not a Redwood internal URL.

Monica Patel: From SDK POV: we’re exposing it as a first-class field (and also a header under the hood) so people can tag requests consistently across languages.

Marissa Cole: This is what powers the Console views like “Top cost drivers by route” and route detail -> model breakdown.

Jada Williams: More concrete definition we’re using in telemetry:
- Prefer SDK-provided route identifier (explicit)
- Else gateway-derived route (when requests go through the Redwood Gateway)
- Else fallback = `unknown`

Amara Diallo: Gateway-derived is basically “best effort” based on incoming HTTP path + method + whatever stable template we can infer.

Amara Diallo: But we really want customers to set it explicitly, because gateways/proxies/frameworks vary wildly.

Thomas Baird: Biggest thing: cardinality. If people put user IDs / UUIDs / timestamps in route names, it will blow up dimensions and we’ll start hashing/rolling up.

Thomas Baird: So please: stable, low-cardinality, human-readable.

Paula Mendes: What’s the recommended naming convention? I’ve seen a few floating around.

Monica Patel: Current guidance draft (works across SDKs):
- Use a small set of “route” strings that match your app’s logical endpoints
- Avoid free-form strings
- Prefer `.` or `/` separators
- Keep it under ~80 chars

Elliot Price: Docs wording we’re planning:
Examples ✅
- `chat.completions`
- `support.summarize_ticket`
- `checkout.calculate_tax`
- `/v1/assistant/chat`

Elliot Price: Examples ❌
- `user/123456/chat`
- `ticket/9f2c0b9a-.../summarize`
- `prompt: summarize my email from ${sender}`

Allison Grant: If you *do* have dynamic paths, template them.
Like `users/:id/profile` not `users/827391/profile`.

Dev Patel: What about teams that have multiple services? Can they include service name?

Logan Wright: Yes, that’s a good pattern. e.g. `billing.invoice_create` or `svc-billing/invoice/create`.

Logan Wright: Just keep it stable + predictable. (Also helps when you do internal chargeback.)

Paula Mendes: Where does “model” fit into this? People are asking if route already implies model.

Jada Williams: Route and model are separate dimensions.
Route is “what workload,” model is “what ran.”
Route detail will show breakdown by model variant (including fallback/reroutes).

Amara Diallo: Important subtlety: smart routing can change the model mid-flight (fallback, region swap). Route should stay the same across that chain.

Thomas Baird: +1 and the route dimension should attach to *every* metering event so cost attribution is consistent even when routing changes.

RedwoodBot: :information_source: Reminder: Please don’t paste customer org IDs or tokens in #general.

Dev Patel: Re: “Unknown route” — what should we tell customers today?

Monica Patel: Usually means they’re not setting the route in the SDK (or they’re calling the raw API without the header).
We’ll have a docs snippet for “how to set route” in Python/TS/Go.

Elliot Price: Also: if they’re using a custom proxy, the gateway can’t infer reliably. Explicit route tagging is the fix.

Allison Grant: Another reason you might see Unknown: older client versions pre-route-tagging support. Updating SDK helps.

Paula Mendes: Are we enforcing any limits?

Thomas Baird: Yes. We’re implementing guardrails:
- normalization (strip weird chars, whitespace)
- length cap
- allowlist-ish character set
- cardinality budgets per org/project per time window
- if exceeded: we bucket into `other` / hashed bucket + surface warning in UI

Marissa Cole: UI will also have a small callout if we’re seeing high unique routes / rollups (so it’s not silent).

Logan Wright: One more: don’t treat route as a “tag everything” dimension.
We’re *not* doing custom dimensions GA yet—route is meant to be the single stable “grouping key” customers can control.

Paula Mendes: Where do people file feedback / edge cases?

Marissa Cole: Best options:
1) #eng-platform for schema/telemetry questions
2) #devex for SDK ergonomics
3) File a Linear issue under the “usage insights” umbrella (PM-612) if it’s product behavior / UI / exports

Dev Patel: For support folks: if it smells like a bug, link the ticket + file Linear with “usage-insights” label. We’ll add canned response text once docs are live.

Elliot Price: Docs feedback can go in #docs too, but please include the exact snippet + what you expected.

Amara Diallo: If anyone has a “weird” routing setup (multi-tenant reverse proxy, service mesh rewriting paths), DM me. I’m collecting cases for gateway derivation.

Allison Grant: SRE note: if you’re load testing and see export timeouts, please keep ranges reasonable (we’re adding hard limits). File #eng-sre if you see sustained failures.

Paula Mendes: Thanks all. I’ll pin a short summary in the announcement once we have the docs link.

Marissa Cole: +1. And if you’re a team that wants to dogfood internally, drop a note—having realistic route naming early helps us avoid painful defaults. :thumbsup:
